title: Concerted handshake scheduler for tensor-pipeline and NCCL coalescing
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description:
Problem: Multi-GPU prefill+decode workloads are exhibiting intermittent tail latency spikes and suboptimal GPU utilization caused by fine-grained handshakes between tensor-parallel and pipeline-parallel stages and many small NCCL collectives. Current runtime issues: (1) kernel selection and launch times are sensitive to small sequence-length variation, (2) KV cache movement and stage syncs create alternating idle/overloaded periods on GPUs, and (3) NCCL is invoked with many small payloads leading to bandwidth inefficiency and increased latency tails.

Goal: Design and implement a "concerted handshake" scheduling layer that: (a) aligns stage handshakes to windowed communication opportunities, (b) coalesces small inter-stage tensors into batched NCCL collectives where safe, (c) exposes a topology-aware micro-batching knob to balance latency vs throughput, and (d) interfaces with kernel selection to choose fusion-friendly kernels when coalescing is enabled. Success metrics are reduced p95/p99 token latency for mixed prefill+decode workloads, improved GPU time-in-use, and higher NCCL effective bandwidth.

Proposed approach:
- Observation & instrumentation (week 1): add fine-grained tracing around prefill/decode stage transitions, kernel selection decision points, and NCCL op sizes. Collect traces from representative workloads (short chat queries + long prefill).
- Scheduler design (weeks 2-4): implement a scheduler component with three capabilities: (1) handshake windowing: create per-request micro-windows (e.g., 0.5–4ms) where handshakes are batched across inflight requests, (2) comm coalescer: accumulate small tensors destined for the same peer and emit a single NCCL op if latency budget allows, (3) topology-aware steering: consult device topology and stage mapping to decide per-window coalescing thresholds.
- Kernel selection integration (week 4): add hints to kernel selector so it can prefer kernels that are friendly to fused/coalesced inputs (e.g., attention kernels that accept concatenated KV blocks).
- Deadlock & fairness controls (week 5): implement safety timeouts, maximum coalesce size, and per-customer fairness quotas so long-running coalescing cannot starve quick requests.
- Testing & benchmark (week 6): microbenchmarks for prefill-only, decode-only, and mixed workloads; large-scale test on dedicated 8xA100 pool.
- Rollout (week 7): canary on a dedicated capacity pool with real traffic; fallback toggles and A/B metrics.

Acceptance criteria:
- p95 token latency drop >= 20% on mixed prefill+decode benchmark vs baseline.
- GPU utilization (active kernels) increase >= 12% without increasing mean latency by > 5%.
- NCCL small-message count reduced by >= 40% and aggregate sustained bandwidth improved.
- No regression in functional correctness (determinism tests, kv-cache validation).

Risks & mitigations:
- Deadlocks if coalescing incorrectly sequences stage dependencies — mitigate with conservative default windows and hard safety timeouts.
- Regression in output ordering for highly interleaved streams — add deterministic reordering layer and strict test vectors.
- Fairness concerns across customers — enforce per-tenant limits and expose opt-out runtime flag.

Observability & metrics to add:
- handshake_window_latency_ms (histogram), coalesced_n_colls, avg_collapsed_payload_bytes, kernel_choice_tag, per-stage-idle_ms, per-request-deadline-breaches.

Related work / dependencies: ENG-27184, ENG-33156, ENG-35912 (reference architectures for topology-aware steering and token routing).

Implementation artifacts: runtime patch to scheduler core (C++), kernel-selector hints (Rust/C++) and user-visible runtime flag (env + Console toggle).

Rollout plan: feature-gated behind runtime-1.22 flag + Console toggle; canary 10% traffic on dedicated pools for 48 hours; monitor p95/p99, NCCL metrics, and request success rate; rollback if regressions exceed thresholds.
